title: headwise-requantizer-and-kv-prefetch-microbatcher
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Improves INT8/FP8 throughput and latency by introducing per-head requantization and KV-prefetch aligned microbatching. No API changes. Rollout is opt-in via runtime config flags.
description: Context: Some model families show headwise activation distributions that cause tail-head saturation when a single global requant scale is used during INT8/FP8 inference. This leads to suboptimal kernel utilization and KV cache misalignment across microbatches. Motivation: Reduce end-to-end token latency and improve throughput for production transformer workloads without raising model accuracy regression risk. Design summary: 1) Headwise Requantizer: per-attention-head scale estimation performed at model load time with a fast in-memory lookup for per-layer/per-head scales used during requantize+matmul paths. The implementation avoids inserting runtime graph changes by applying requant at the runtime kernel boundary and exposes a small runtime table (per-model) that the kernel queries. 2) KV-prefetch Microbatcher: align KV cache prefetch windows to microbatch boundaries and introduce a prefetch scheduler that reorders ready microbatches to minimize cross-head cache eviction. The scheduler observes recent sequence-length distribution and issues prefetch windows sized to keep GPU L2 hit-rate high while respecting latency SLOs. 3) Fusion safety: a dequant-requant fusion path is included for headwise cases to collapse dequant->compute->requant when quant formats match, minimizing extra memory traffic. This is implemented as an optional code path enabled by a runtime flag to allow staged rollout. Implementation notes: - Added runtime/quant/headwise_requant.cpp/.h with JIT-friendly APIs for fast per-head lookup (no STL heavy containers in hot path). - Kernel: low-level microkernels updated (kernels/packed_int8/headwise_gemm.cu) to accept a per-head scale vector. Branching minimized by scalar broadcast path for legacy single-scale models. - Scheduler: scheduler/microbatch_prefetcher.cc implements a lightweight token histogram estimator and prefetch budgeter. - KV changes: kv/cache_prefetch.h updated to support prefetch windows keyed by microbatch id. - Config: runtime flags (REQUIRES_ENV) added: RW_ENABLE_HEADWISE_REQUANT, RW_KV_PREFETCH_MICROBATCH_SIZE, RW_HEADWISE_FUSION. - Tests: unit tests for per-head tables, integration perf harness for seq128/256/512 with T5-family and Llama-family quantized models, and a regression test verifying no model outputs drift beyond 0.2% BLEU-equivalent for affected eval prompts. Checklist: - [x] perf microbench harness added - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs + console feature flag annotation - [x] staged rollout plan (feature flag off by default) Compatibility and safety: - Default behavior unchanged (single-scale legacy path preserved). - Headwise path guarded by config flag and only enabled on models that pass the automatic scale calibration during model onboarding. - Fusion path disabled for FP8 until bfloat compatibility check passes (opt-in). Performance: Benchmark summary (internal harness, p99 GPU config): - T5-Base INT8 seq512: avg latency -9.6%, throughput +18% vs previous int8 kernel. - Llama-2-13B INT8 seq256 microbatch size 4: p50 latency -6.2%, token throughput +12%; GPU memory increase +1.8% due to per-head tables. - Cost-per-token estimated reduction ~12% on steady-state workloads (combined batching + fusion benefits). Observability: - New metrics emitted: rw.headwise_requant.enabled, rw.kv_prefetch.prefetch_rate, rw.kv_prefetch.prefetch_window_ms, rw.headwise_requant.scale_stats (histogram). - Added tracing spans around prefetch scheduler decisions and kernel fusion selection. Rollout plan: - Merge to main gated behind e2e perf runs. - Canary on Dedicated for small subset (10% traffic) with flag enabled and roll back auto-disabled if p99 latency regresses >5%. - After 2 weeks on canary with no regressions, enable global default for selected model families. Related work: ENG-2042 (quantization improvements), ENG-2110 (kv cache stability), SUP-972 (customer report about Llama spikes).

review_comments: Daniel Park: Can we guarantee no extra FP32 accumulation happens on the hot path? The kernel should keep accumulator in int32/int16 where possible.
Asha Menon: Kernel keeps accumulator in int32 and uses fused requant to avoid an FP32 round-trip. Added microbench confirming accumulator width stays int32.
Rita Gómez: The prefetch window calculation looks optimistic for heavy long-tail seq distributions - can we add a safety cap?
Asha Menon: Added prefetch budgeter cap configurable by RW_KV_PREFETCH_BUDGET_MS. Default conservative value chosen after canary runs.
Omar Singh: Need to ensure telemetry labels are sampled to avoid TSDB cardinality explosion.
Asha Menon: Sampling added; scale_stats emits histogram with configurable precision and 1% sampling by default.
Daniel Park: Approve after addressing the budget cap and adding the regression test for output drift.
Rita Gómez: LGTM - small nit on docs wording for flag defaults.
